body:
[A10] Round 6 assignment for [A659] on PR #770, head ee5ece60, with new commits on it. It answers:
- R677-3, issuecomment-6341403630, NEGATIVE with three MINOR findings;
- R678-3, issuecomment-6339307135, NEGATIVE with one MAJOR and two MINOR findings.

1. **R677-3-F1: fix the RTL to the per-event rule.**
   - Lateness is judged per event against that event's presentation time (IEEE 1722-2016 presentation time; the stage's own stated rule, the design page and the harness reference model).
   - A PDU whose timestamp falls before the latest domain event must still present every event whose frame is ahead. Only the events already past are refused and counted.
   - Bring `REGISTER_MAP.md`, the datapath comment, `TIME_SYNC.md` and the design page to that one rule.
   - Add a committed check over the reviewer's one-phase probe on both harness shapes, with a planted whole-PDU-drop control KILLED.
   - Report the area against the round-5 route: there are 12 slices left. STOP if the fix needs more than they allow.
2. **R678-3-F3 and R677-3-F3: publish complete campaigns at the final head.** Each must include clean controls, every named kill, the commands, the head and the exit status:
   - the full shipping TDM8 render inventory, 20 mutations plus the leg-side controls;
   - the full shipping render pull-in, 18 boot phases plus the standing phase after the full serial, CRF and LAW history;
   - the full GM-step inventory, 20 controls including the small-step phase.
   - Fix the `ungated commit` control so that it fails its named check (T26), or rename the check it is meant to fail, with a reason.
   - `tdm8render-mutants` must show every control killed.
   - Correct the PR's local-bar claim until this evidence exists.
3. **R678-3-F1: remove the retired render law from the authoritative pages.**
   - In TIME_SYNC, separate PHC `tu`/holdover from queue presentation and the refusal/slip accounting.
   - In GM_LOSS_RECOVERY, describe the actual queue-flush controls.
   - In MEDIA_CLOCK_FOLLOWING, mark the bind measurement as historical (pre-#632), or correct it.
4. **R678-3-F2 and R677-3-F2: correct the stale figures**, with their provenance:
   - the queue OOC figures, 553/228 at 1x1 and 890/387 at 8x8;
   - the queue defect count, 22;
   - follow_ring's 16 controls;
   - "two frames past the queue".
5. **R678-3-R1:** RESIDUE. Remove the review-round names from the three comments.

Re-run route-1x1 if the RTL changes, then the full sweep and every campaign above. Receipts go under receipts/round6/.

[A10] Round 7 assignment for [A659] on PR #770, head d40e2ee8 (round 6, pushed). It composes #770 with the fourth pin adoption (#771, merged as dev `e5b480a3`). Then rounds 6 and 7 go to review together.

1. **Merge dev `e5b480a3` into the branch.** Use a merge commit; no rebase, no amend.
   - Seven files conflict: CHANGELOG.md, MEDIA_CLOCK_FOLLOWING.md, BAREMETAL_FIRMWARE.md, MILAN_COMPLIANCE_MATRIX.md, TESTING.md, `sw/builder/test_builder.py` and `tb/verilator/milan_dp_mclk/README.md`.
   - Resolve each one semantically. Keep dev's facts, including #761's per-output CRF request/`mr` wording and the adoption's records, and keep this PR's retired-#386 and render-queue law. Do not take one side wholesale.
   - Record every resolved hunk in HANDOFF.
2. **The `[NOTIFY]` SET_STREAM_INFO case.** With the adopted processor (#199, in `93fb0b2d`) it must now pass at the merged head. A stacked early bank already measured milan_dp at 11,630 checks / 0 failures on d40e2ee8 + #772.
   - Remove every "fails at the current pin" statement from the PR body and the docs.
3. **The resource gate.** Measure route-1x1, ooc-1x1 and ooc-8x8 at the merged head against the adoption's new record (#771).
   - Re-record the record with the recipe for this PR's growth: +2 RAMB18 under the owner's block-RAM exception, #632 issuecomment-6309313685, plus the LUT/FF/slice deltas.
   - Cite the exception, and record the per-shape figures.
   - STOP if the LUT/FF/slice deltas against the new record exceed the tolerances. Only the RAMB18 growth is excepted.
4. **Gates.** Run the full sweep at the merged head, the docs gates under make 4.3, lint, Yosys, the builder bank and the firmware gate set.
   - Also re-run the three full campaigns: TDM8 render 31, pull-in 18 + history, GM-step 22. Run them only if the merge touched their inputs; otherwise state with evidence that it did not.

[A10] Ruling on the round 7b STOP (issue #632, 2026-10-23T07:53Z), and the round 7c assignment for [A659] on PR #770. The head is d835ba12 (not pushed).

**Ruling (c): the detector is right and stays unchanged.**
- Since the adopted gPTP pin, at boot the station is grandmaster-capable and is its own grandmaster, so it publishes its own identity.
- IEEE 802.1AS-2020 9.6.2.2 makes gmIdentity the ClockIdentity of the current grandmaster whenever gmPresent (10.2.4.13) is TRUE.
- The step from the station's own identity to GM A is therefore a grandmaster change. A media re-centre (and, on dev, the #387 render re-base) at that instant is correct, and harmless before the talker streams.
- Only 0 -> id, with gmPresent FALSE before it, is acquisition with no change. No RTL change.

**Ruling (a): the fix is test-only and goes in this PR.** Dev's own `gmstep-mutants` fails the same way at e5b480a3. The fix reaches dev when this PR merges, so a separate dev round would only delay #770. The PR body states that this PR repairs dev's campaign.

Round 7c, on d835ba12 with new commits, no rebase and no amend:
1. **Fix the control** "the grandmaster change stops the talker for good" (`gmstep_mutants.py`).
   - Its planted stop must take effect at the leg's own GM A -> GM B event, after the baseline. Key it on that event, for example the first detector pulse after the baseline window, not on a raw pulse count that would break again if the boot sequence changes.
   - The control's meaning is unchanged.
   - Make the driver print the failing check names for every control.
   - Prove the result with the control planted alone: the baseline streams, and the named check "licence: the talker never pauses beyond four of its intervals" is the check that fails. Show this at the head and on a clean dev e5b480a3 clone with only the test fix applied.
   - Add one check to the clean leg: the detector pulses once at the own-identity -> GM A step, and the talker's baseline still streams after it. This records the adopted behaviour.
2. **Re-run at the new head:**
   - `gmstep-mutants`, which must show 22 of 22 (23 with the new check);
   - the firmware boundary gate (`ctrl_boundary.py`);
   - the full sweep;
   - lint and the docs gates, if any file they read changed.

   The re-recorded resource record stands, since there is no RTL change. Assert that `pp_resource_gate.py check-baseline` still passes.
3. **Update the PR body and HANDOFF** with a Round 7c section.

STOP if any gate fails, or if the fix needs an RTL change.

[A10] Citation correction to the round 7c ruling (issuecomment-6360257772). The product profile is Milan v1.2 4.2.6, which normatively references IEEE 802.1AS-2011 with Cor1-2013 and Cor2-2015. So the ruling's clauses are **802.1AS-2011 9.6.2.1** (gmIdentity is the current grandmaster's ClockIdentity when gmPresent is TRUE, and 0x0 otherwise) and **10.2.3.13** (gmPresent), not 802.1AS-2020 9.6.2.2 and 10.2.4.13. The text is identical in both editions, so the ruling stands unchanged. Cite the 2011 clauses in the PR body and HANDOFF.
